import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivDegree
import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.Ledger.ResidueDegree

/-!
# Positivity of effective curve-divisor degree

This is the numerical leaf needed by the D2 Grassmannian route: a nonzero
effective divisor on a smooth integral curve has strictly positive weighted
degree.  The proof keeps the residue-degree weights explicit, so it applies
over an arbitrary field.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open AlgebraicGeometry

namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CurveDivisor

variable {K : Type u} [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}}
  [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
  [IsIntegral X]
  [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]

/-- A nonzero effective divisor has positive residue-weighted degree. -/
theorem deg_pos_of_nonneg_of_ne_zero {D : X.CurveDivisor}
    (hD : 0 ≤ D) (hne : D ≠ 0) : 0 < deg K D := by
  classical
  let d : {x : X // x ≠ genericPoint X} →₀ ℤ := D
  obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ : ∃ p : {x : X // x ≠ genericPoint X}, d p ≠ 0 := by
    by_contra h
    apply hne
    exact Finsupp.ext (fun p => by
      by_contra hp
      exact h ⟨p, hp⟩)
  have hp0 : 0 ≤ d p := hD p
  have hp1 : 0 < d p := lt_of_le_of_ne hp0 (Ne.symm hp)
  have hres : 0 < (X.residueDeg K p.1 : ℤ) := by
    exact_mod_cast residueDeg_pos (K := K) p.2
  rw [deg]
  rw [Finsupp.sum]
  have hsum : 0 ≤ ∑ q ∈ d.support.erase p,
      d q * (X.residueDeg K q.1 : ℤ) := by
    exact Finset.sum_nonneg fun q _ =>
      mul_nonneg (hD q) (Int.natCast_nonneg _)
  have hterm : 0 < d p * (X.residueDeg K p.1 : ℤ) := by
    exact mul_pos hp1 hres
  rw [← Finset.sum_erase_add _ _ (Finsupp.mem_support_iff.mpr hp)]
  linarith

end AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CurveDivisor
